pr_body:
Replaces https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/68456
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/68454 (?)
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/62756

Increase entropy in randomly generated file names
Pass through caller method name and line number in more cases to improve test file name forensics
Add # prefix to test folders to make it easier to find leaks in today's crowded temp folders
Remove any read-only attributes on files within the test folder to ensure it can be deleted
Fix several test issues causing leaked files
Improve file-matching test to ensure it doesn't accidentally match a randomly generated name
Fixup sudo conditions
In some cases, a test was leaking its temp directory when it remote-exec'd code that changed the current directory to the temp directory. The fix was to set the current directory back at the end of the remote-exec'd code. This is a puzzle as the test directory gets deleted when the test method completes, which happens after the remote-exec process has already quit, and the current-directory of the remote-exec process ought to be irrelevant. It's as if Windows holds on to it a little longer.

This fixes almost all leaked files when running the FileSystem test cases.

review_comments: Can you please elaborate on why this is needed?

the new directory has FileAttributes.Normal, there's no need to read them.

if you mean - why bother setting them back - it's because a r/o directory can't be deleted. this was before I went in an added code in the cleanup to handle this, but it seems reasonable cleanup here.
I mean, before we were restoring `Attributes` to its `original` value, I don't see how `original` could contain the `ReadOnly` flag if the directory was just created one line above.
It couldn't, but it was an extra line of code.
Oh, I see your point. In this case I guess I did it only for cleanup - remove the extra line.
This static also exists in ProcessTests.Unix.cs, should it be on a common class instead (PlatformDetection.Unix.cs)?
It can't go in PlatformDetection as not all projects that include PlatformDetection also reference the remote executor.

It no longer checks `RemoteExecutor.IsSupported`, is that ok?
Also, you already know is Unix because `ProcessTests.Unix.cs` only compiles for it.
Ah, I see, these tests weren't actually using RemoteExecutor.
I think an analyzer-codefix for a standalone call to `File.Create(path)` would be very helpful to avoid these mistakes. Not many people realize that it returns a disposable FileStream.

It should be found if you change CS2000 to "warn"
https://github.com/danmoseley/runtime/blob/4225cb0fff263e9fbc7ad007ab18e774a1b73d1e/eng/CodeAnalysis.test.globalconfig#L409
CA2213 is also relevant.

@stephentoub did you try these -- was there a lot of noise?

> The fix was to set the current directory back at the end of the remote-exec'd code.

you mean set it back to the path we previously set in `ChangeCurrentDirectory()`? If so, I think this should be `Directory.SetCurrentDirectory(tempCwd)`

We don't want that -- tempCwd is within the test's folder, which we want cleaned up.

(As I mentioned in the description, I don't understand why the current directory of the child process is relevant since by the time the test exits, the remoteexec process has quit and presumably the OS closed any handles it had open. But nevertheless that is what I saw.)

Ah I see what you mean, sounds like the folder is still locked by the RemoteExecutor process. 
I don't know if it may be possible to change the CWD of the RemoteExecutor Process in, say, `RemoteInvokeHandle.Dispose()` in order to avoid doing this each time its cwd gets changed.

That may be cleaner.

@jkotas do you have any idea why resetting the current directory seems necessary, given the remote exec process exits before we clean up the test folder?
created https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/pull/9200

> @jkotas do you have any idea why resetting the current directory seems necessary, given the remote exec process exits before we clean up the test folder?

My guess is that it is likely anti-virus, watson or some other kind of Windows background task holding the directory. I think that it is unlikely for the process itself to be holding onto the directory once it exists.
Just curious, what might happen if you don't `lock` it?

The Random class is not thread safe - and this is a static method accessed from any thread running a test. (We do have Random.Shared which is thread safe, but it's not available when targeting .NET Framework)
Should we use other prefix instead (TMP_)?
I chose # as it only makes the paths 1 char longer. We have had length problems in the past - hence the code in FileCleanupTestBase that shortens paths. Plus, nobody else seems to use #..
Why do you need larger names?

this will fail whenever the test file name contains two capital B's in a row. previously that didn't happen as GUID letters formatted as lower case. Initially I was using capital letters in the generated names so it failed approx every 200 runs. I changed to lower case for some reason but seemed reasonable to make it longer in case we change again.
Sounds quite hard to figure out when an issue reporting the failing test gets filed. Consider adding a comment.
Sure. I'll do that in another PR rather than reset validation again.
